sections.html:
Lake Michigan borders Porter County on the north and the Kankakee River on the south, in Indiana's northwest corner. Valparaiso is the seat, Portage is the second city and the biggest by both people and land, and the 2020 census found 173,215 residents. Nine towns fill in the map: Beverly Shores, Burns Harbor, Chesterton, Dune Acres, Hebron, Kouts, Ogden Dunes, Porter and Town of Pines. Twelve townships carry the assessment work: Boone, Center, Jackson, Liberty, Morgan, Pine, Pleasant, Portage, Porter, Union, Washington and Westchester.

A parcel might lie in a city, a town, a township alone or a lakeshore community, and each combination has its own levy mix. A house on the water in Ogden Dunes and a farmhouse near Kouts pay the same county treasurer, yet their statements can look nothing alike.

Start with the TS-1A that arrives with your bill, then match your problem to one of three county offices.

QuestionOfficeContact
Assessment went upAssessor, 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 211, Valparaiso(219) 465-3460
A deduction dropped offAuditor(219) 465-3445; Auditor@porterco.org
Payment posted wrongTreasurer, 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso(219) 465-3470

Rate changes come from the state, so none of these offices can alter the rate. Sellers should also check with the Auditor that the homestead deduction is on file, because a buyer's lender reads the same record.

Each year has a spring bill due May 10 and a fall bill due November 10, and a weekend or holiday date rolls forward a business day. A bill under $25.00 is billed whole instead of split. Full and partial payments are taken all year, and anything late draws a penalty.

Timeliness is judged by postmark: a correctly addressed envelope stamped by the U.S. Postal Service on or before the due date is on time, and so is one an express carrier received by then. Penalty rules are in Indiana Code 6-1.1-37-10, and your bill shows the calculation on its front.

  • Online through the county's two payment portals: electronic checks carry no extra charge and cards carry a processing fee.
  • By phone or mail, following the county's payment pages. Address mail to the Treasurer, 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso, IN 46383, and leave the check unattached to the coupon.
  • At the Treasurer's counter.
  • Through a mortgage, escrow or title company, each of which has its own electronic portfolio system.

An online payment needs at least two days to post, so the lookup page can still show a balance for a bit. Account history updates nightly. Surplus claim forms go out after the June and December settlements if you overpay, and a spring overpayment is applied to the fall amount.

Unpaid parcels are offered in an online auction on zeusauction.com. An owner who wants a property withdrawn has to get cash or certified funds to the Treasurer at 155 Indiana Avenue, Suite 209 by the cutoff in that year's notice, which falls the day before bidding starts.

A sold property can still be bought back. The price is 110 percent of the minimum bid in the first six months and 115 percent later, with any overbid added along with 5 percent annual interest on it, and with any later taxes the buyer paid. Buyers of certificates in the 2026 sale hold them until Friday, October 22, 2027, and that is the last day to redeem. A sale above the minimum bid with no redemption can leave the former owner of record owed the surplus.

A tax sale payment plan is open to some taxpayers. A property that goes unsold but is pursued for title has a 120 day redemption window. Redemption questions go to the Auditor at (219) 465-3449, and payment plan questions to the Treasurer at taxquestions@porterco.org.

An appeal opens with Form 130, one per parcel, filed with the assessing official, who is the county Assessor wherever there is no township assessor. For the current assessment, June 15 of the assessment year is the date when the notice went out before May 1. When it went out on or after May 1, the date is June 15 of the year statements are mailed.

A narrower error correction route allows a filing up to three years after the taxes were first due. No evidence is needed to file. Both sides trade what they have at a preliminary informal meeting.

  • When the meeting settles nothing, the county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals holds a hearing within 180 days of filing and gives you at least 30 days of notice.
  • From there you can carry the result to the Indiana Board of Tax Review on Form 131 inside 45 days.
  • The Indiana Tax Court is the last stop, and the same 45 days run from the board's final decision.

Indiana caps a bill at a share of gross assessed value. Homesteads that carry the standard deduction stop at 1 percent, other residential and agricultural land at 2 percent, and nonresidential and personal property at 3 percent. Any calculated tax above the cap is wiped out by a circuit breaker credit.

SEA 1, the 2025 reform, is changing the deduction mix. After 2026 the $48,000 standard deduction shrinks every year while the supplemental deduction grows, and a homestead credit of 10 percent of the bill, up to $300, starts in 2026. Results depend on home value, so look at your own statement before you promise a buyer a tax figure.

sections.h2: Selling a Porter County house with taxes due
sections.html:
First, ask the Treasurer for the parcel's balance and decide how it gets paid at closing. Title companies want unpaid tax cleared at the closing table, and a property on the certified list owes the redemption amount, not just the base tax.

  • Compare the bill with the online balance to see whether the spring or fall installment is still open.
  • Find out from the Auditor if a deduction on the parcel ends with the sale.
  • For a house on the tax sale list, get the redemption figure and ask about the payment plan.
  • Report any open appeal to the title company.

A sale that falls between due dates can leave one installment open, so ask the title company how it will be divided at closing. Houses near the lakefront or the South Shore Line stations tend to attract different buyers than rural homes in the south, and that changes how quickly a house sells and how much wear buyers will tolerate.

Cash buyers can close despite a tax problem, because the title company pays the balance or redemption amount from your proceeds and you need not find the money beforehand. With no lender appraisal, a house that needs repairs is priced on its condition and is not held up waiting for a loan.

faqs.q: What are the Porter County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: May 10 for spring and November 10 for fall. If either falls on a weekend or holiday it slides to the next business day, and a postmark dated on or before it counts.

faqs.q: Where do I mail a Porter County tax payment?
faqs.a: Mail the coupon and check to the Treasurer at 155 Indiana Ave, Suite 209, Valparaiso, IN 46383, without stapling or clipping them together. A self-addressed stamped envelope brings back a receipt in about six to eight weeks.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a higher assessment in Porter County?
faqs.a: The Assessor, at (219) 465-3460. A dropped deduction goes to the Auditor at (219) 465-3445, and a misposted payment to the Treasurer at (219) 465-3470.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Porter County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes. The delinquent tax and costs must be paid first or redeemed afterward. Get the payoff from the Treasurer and the redemption figure from the Auditor, then have the title company list the amount at closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an assessment in Porter County?
faqs.a: Usually by June 15 for the current assessment, with the year depending on when your notice was mailed. Error corrections can be filed up to three years after the taxes were first due.
